brief: Goldman Sachs morning compilation across five desks. On US rates, Sehgal reads Chairman Warsh and Governor Waller as starkly different, calls the hike a coin toss, and rules out a full hiking cycle because housing is in recession while AI CapEx booms, so he pairs a short duration position in the belly with long risk assets. Brown notes September sits at 15 bps priced after a strong payroll report, puts the hike versus hold bar near 25 bps core PCE, and favors scaling into front end longs on back-ups. On JPY, a 3% rally is attributed to expected domestic policy shifts and intervention risk. Ueda has confirmed September BoJ hike pricing and GPIF reallocation speculation has grown, so FX Strategy sees a stronger tactical long JPY case and short USD/JPY as a pro-risk hedge, while warning that inflow anticipation may be disappointed. Tokyo strats counter that BoJ pricing has limited hawkish room and that GPIF needs a 10y JGB near 3.5% to repatriate. Coppersmith argues AI matters more for stocks than next week's inflation data, with the weekly SPX straddle at ~1%, semiconductor implied vol halved and tech momentum down 50%. Week ahead forecasts follow.
